chunks: We were informed by Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ghalib, who said: We were told by Abu al-Fadl Ya'qub ibn Yusuf, who said: We were told by Abd al-Rahman, who said: We were told by Mu'adh ibn Hisham, who said: My father told me, from Mu'ammar, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Dhamdam, from Abu Huraira, that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his Family) ordered the killing of the two blacks during prayer.
Mu'ammar said: I said to Yahya: And what is the meaning of the two blacks? He said: The snake and the scorpion.

key_terms.الْأَسْوَدَيْنِ: The two blacks (referring to snake and scorpion)

ai.seo_question: What are the 'two blacks' mentioned in the hadith regarding prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* clarifies the specific identity of the 'two blacks' (al-Aswadani) as the snake and scorpion, resolving ambiguity in legal texts regarding what may be killed during prayer. It establishes the permissibility of breaking wudu or prayer posture to eliminate these specific pests, reflecting the practical jurisprudence of the Imams in balancing ritual purity with environmental necessity. The hadith underscores the principle that minor disruptions to prayer are permissible when dealing with creatures that pose a direct threat or distraction.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were informed by Abu’l-Hasan, Ahmad bin Muhammed bin Ahmad bin Ghalib, that he said: We were told by Abu’l-Fadl, Ya’qoub bin Yusuf, that he said: We were told by Abdul-Rahman, that he said: We were told by Mu’adh bin Hisham, that he said: I was told by my father, from Mu’ammar, from Yahya bin Abi Katheer, from Dhamdham, from Abu Huraira, that the Prophet, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, ordered to kill the two blacks during prayer.
Mu’ammar said: I said to Yahya: And what is the meaning of the two blacks? He said: The snake and the scorpion.
